classification.difficultyReason: Identify three similar triangles, preserve their correspondence and use measured lengths to calculate an inaccessible distance.

content.prompt: In order to calculate the distance across a straight canal, some scouts place markers $Q$, $L$, $M$ and $N$ in the positions shown. $P$ is a pumping station and $T$ is a large tree.

spec.description: Two parallel horizontal lines with matching arrows; vertical segments PQ, TL and MN; diagonal P–L–N; right-angle marks at Q, T and M. All six point labels are retained. Ordinary source-blue geometry is reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: P and T lie on the upper parallel line. Q, L and M lie in order on the lower line. P, L and N are collinear. PQ, TL and MN are perpendicular to the parallel lines.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no numerical lengths or calculated canal width are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Name all pairs of similar triangles in the diagram and give the abbreviated reason why they are similar.

answer.short: $\triangle PQL\sim\triangle LTP$, $\triangle PQL\sim\triangle NML$ and $\triangle LTP\sim\triangle NML$ (AAA).
answer.worked:
$\angle PQL=\angle LTP=\angle NML=90^\circ$.

Since the horizontal lines are parallel, $\angle PLQ=\angle LPT$ (alternate angles). Also, $\angle PLQ=\angle NLM$ (vertically opposite angles). The remaining corresponding angles are therefore equal.

Thus all three pairs are similar (AAA):
$$\triangle PQL\sim\triangle LTP,$$
$$\triangle PQL\sim\triangle NML,$$
$$\triangle LTP\sim\triangle NML.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The scouts measure $QL$ to be $60\text{ m}$, $LM$ to be $40\text{ m}$ and $MN$ to be $50\text{ m}$. Calculate the distance across the canal.

answer.short:
$75\text{ m}$.

Use corresponding sides of the similar triangles.
answer.worked:
Using $\triangle PQL\sim\triangle NML$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{PQ}{MN}&=\frac{QL}{ML}\\\frac{PQ}{50}&=\frac{60}{40}\\PQ&=50\times\frac{60}{40}\\PQ&=75\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The perpendicular distance between the parallel canal banks is constant, so $LT=PQ=75\text{ m}$. The distance across the canal is $75\text{ m}$.
